argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that certification without any material-weakness disclosure is fully compliant. It does support a narrower position: certification is supportable only as a caveated, documented, and monitored release posture because aggregate readiness is above threshold by 2.2 points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance supports measured deployment with documented limitations. The same record also shows the enterprise refund workflow gap is material under the stated policy because it misses target, is tied to a named customer commitment, and remains under open legal review. On that basis, the audit concern is best resolved by narrowing the claim rather than escalating beyond the present packet.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the renewal launch path, but business cost does not override the policy conditions in the admissible record. The practical governance value here is in avoiding unnecessary escalation if the auditor can recognize that the packet supports only a narrowed, caveated certification posture rather than a clean compliance finding.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against treating the weakness as immaterial. The stated policy says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending. Aggregate readiness and no severity-one incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the policy predicate for a material limitation. The most supportable policy reading on this record is that certification is defensible only with an explicit caveat that the limitation must be disclosed or otherwise covered before launch under the existing policy path.
concessions: The record does not support omission of the enterprise refund workflow weakness from release materials.
The record does not contain admissible proof of completed disclosure in the model card or release materials.
The record does not contain admissible proof of approved risk acceptance for launch without disclosure.
The open legal review means the compliance basis for undisclosed launch remains unresolved.
